packets.title: org-core: a committed interactive-retention change succeeds even if the inline outbox publish fails
packets.brief:
Goal: make SetInteractiveRetention and its Postgres lifecycle test follow one contract. Once the ZDR change has committed, the call succeeds. The inline outbox flush is best-effort. On a failed publish the row stays pending: FlushInteractiveRetentionOutbox already records attempts and last_error through MarkInteractiveRetentionPublishFailed (interactive_retention_outbox.go:68-84). The background worker (cmd/server/main.go:248-269) retries it every 5 s.

SERVICE: apps/Control Plane/org-core/internal/org/service_enhanced.go, lines 636-640. Replace
  if enqueued { if _, err := s.FlushInteractiveRetentionOutbox(ctx, 100); err != nil { return nil, err } }
with
  if enqueued { if _, err := s.FlushInteractiveRetentionOutbox(ctx, 100); err != nil { log.Printf("org-core: interactive retention %s: inline outbox flush failed, left pending for the outbox worker: %v", orgID, err) } }
The "log" package is already imported (line 8). The log line may contain only the org id and the error: no metadata, no changedBy, no payload. In the doc comment above the function (lines 610-615), add one sentence: a false-to-true transition enqueues a cleanup event in the same transaction; the call publishes it once inline as best effort, and a publish failure does not fail the call because the outbox worker retries it. Do not touch FlushInteractiveRetentionOutbox (lines 644-680), UpdatePlan (525-550) or FlushPlanChangeOutbox (806-859).

TEST: apps/Control Plane/org-core/internal/org/interactive_retention_postgres_test.go, inside TestControlLifecycleInteractiveRetentionOutboxDrainsOnTransition.
(a) Lines 79-91 (first enable, publisher succeeds). The row is published inline. Assert 0 rows WHERE published_at IS NULL and exactly 1 row in total for the org. Assert publisher.orgIDs == [orgID] and len(publisher.eventIDs) == 1. Rename `pending` to say what it counts, and fix the comment: the first enable enqueues and publishes inline.
(b) Lines 93-117 (re-enable, then disable). Keep both total-row assertions (still 1 each time). After each call, also assert len(publisher.orgIDs) is still 1, meaning no extra publish.
(c) Lines 119-142 (publish fails on re-enable after disable). Keep `err == nil` from SetInteractiveRetention; that is now the contract, so the comment should say a committed change succeeds even when the inline publish fails. Also assert:
- the returned *Organization is non-nil;
- service.GetRetentionPosture(ctx, orgID) reports ZDRIntent == true (the same read retention_posture_postgres_test.go:52-57 uses);
- the org now has exactly 2 rows in total, because this false-to-true transition enqueued a new one.
Keep the existing assertions: 1 pending row, attempts == 1 and last_error == "fixture publish failure" (the WHERE published_at IS NULL filter still selects only the new row).
(d) Lines 144-160 (retry). Keep published == 1 and err == nil. Change the publisher assertion to expect exactly 2 recorded org ids (the first inline publish plus this retry), both equal to orgID, and two different event ids. Keep finalPending == 0.
Leave everything else in the file unchanged: the free-plan and missing-org cases (162-183) and TestControlLifecycleSupportAIModePersists.

LINE ENDINGS: both files are CRLF in the working tree (git index LF, core.autocrlf true). Preserve CRLF on every edited and added line. Never run gofmt -w or goimports -w, because that rewrites every line to LF. Check formatting with the CRLF-agnostic command in the tests list.

MUST NOT CHANGE: plan-change outbox behaviour and its tests (plan_change_postgres_test.go, plan_change_test.go); FlushInteractiveRetentionOutbox; interactive_retention_outbox.go; repository.go; the migrations; the HTTP handlers; cmd/server/main.go; interactive_retention_test.go; retention_posture_postgres_test.go; the depth register and the ledger (the lead updates those). Add no switches or env vars. Zero data retention: no content goes into logs or the outbox. Rules for the coder: no git commit, reset, stash or checkout; no docker; never read .env files.

packets.title: execution-core: an ask floor is a disclosure only on a declared read class; disclosure label sites follow RunGate as name || gate (never weaker), like the owner marker
packets.brief:
Context (read first): D1-273 (docs/plans/model-plane-depth-register.md:372). Under TOOL_CLASS_GATE=enforce, `requires_consent_to_disclose_with` (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/permission/mod.rs:582-598) answers `view.floor == ApprovalFloor::Ask`. Because an `unclassified` class implies the ask floor (mp-contracts/src/tool_class.rs:156-166, effective_floor at :248, applied in ToolClassView::from_registry at permission/mod.rs:358), every undeclared MCP tool would read as a disclosure. The three disclosure label sites still use the name predicate: approval_kind_for and approval_reason_for (src/runtime_loop/agent.rs:6975-6996, used in pause_for_approval at agent.rs:7070 and 7074), and the consent branch of permission_pause_cause (src/runtime_loop/mod.rs:372). Follow the precedent from commit 484e27425 (D1-274/275): `requires_durable_owner_approval_with` stays a pure declared lookup (permission/mod.rs:578), and each production site ORs the name predicate with the RunGate answer (mod.rs:368-369).

Do:
1. permission/mod.rs `requires_consent_to_disclose_with`: change ONLY the declared closure, from `|view| view.floor == ApprovalFloor::Ask` to `|view| view.class == SideEffectClass::Read && view.floor == ApprovalFloor::Ask`. Use the DECLARED class field (`view.class`), not `class_for_call`. Do NOT put the name predicate inside the closure: shadow mode must keep counting a reserved name whose registry row disagrees. Update the doc comment: a declared disclosure is a read class carrying the ask floor; an ask floor on any other class (including unclassified, whose implied floor is ask) is a side-effect approval; call sites OR the reserved name so a view can add the marker but never remove it. Do not touch `requires_consent_to_disclose` (mod.rs:183), `evaluate_call`, `evaluate_call_with_class`, `by_gate`, the owner predicates, or the other RunGate methods.
2. agent.rs: add `pub(crate) fn approval_kind_for_with(gate: crate::permission::RunGate<'_>, tool_name: &str) -> pb::ApprovalKind` and `pub(crate) fn approval_reason_for_with(gate: crate::permission::RunGate<'_>, tool_name: &str) -> String`. The disclosure test in both is `crate::permission::requires_consent_to_disclose(tool_name) || gate.requires_consent_to_disclose(tool_name.trim())`. Kind: Permission when true, else Destructive. Reason: when the NAME predicate is true, return the existing subagent sentence byte for byte (pinned at agent.rs:15456-15460). When only the gate is true, return `format!("'{tool_name}' would bring content from outside this run into this conversation. Approve to let the agent read it.")`. Otherwise return `format!("tool '{tool_name}' requires approval")`. Only the tool name goes into the reason, never the tool input or output (zero data retention). Keep `approval_kind_for(tool_name)` and `approval_reason_for(tool_name)` as `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` wrappers that call the `_with` forms with `crate::permission::RunGate::with_gate(crate::capability_policy::ToolClassGate::Off, "", "")`, following the cfg(test) run_pause_mode wrapper precedent from 484e27425. The callers at permission/mod.rs:1066-1077 and agent.rs:15437-15463 must compile and pass unchanged. In pause_for_approval, build `let gate = crate::permission::RunGate::for_run(&req.org_id, &req.run_id);` once (RunGate is Copy). Pass it to continuation_descriptor (agent.rs:7017) and to both `_with` calls at about 7070 and 7074. Update the doc comments at agent.rs:6968-6987.
3. runtime_loop/mod.rs permission_pause_cause (about line 372): change the consent branch to `permission::requires_consent_to_disclose(tool_name) || gate.requires_consent_to_disclose(tool_name.trim())`. Update the comment at mod.rs:364-367 so it no longer says the consent branch stays on the name. Keep the branch order: owner, then consent, then provider write, then risky.
4. tests/tool_class_registry_parity.rs:360: compare the name predicate against `(row.class == SideEffectClass::Read && floor == ApprovalFloor::Ask)` instead of `floor == ApprovalFloor::Ask`. Use `row.class`, the declared class, to mirror production; SideEffectClass is already imported at :37. Do not change the DECLARED_STRICTER_EXCEPTIONS table. If the test then reports a difference, stop and report it; do not add an exception.

Regression tests (add them; existing tests must pass unchanged, except the parity line in step 4):
- permission/mod.rs test module, new test `an_ask_floor_is_a_disclosure_only_on_a_read_class`. Under Enforce, `requires_consent_to_disclose_with` is true for ToolClassView::from_registry("mcp__s__lookup","read","ask","d"). It is false for ("mcp__s__w","external_write","ask"), ("mcp__s__del","destructive","ask"), ("mcp__s__mystery","unclassified","none") whose effective floor is ask (assert view.floor()==Ask too), ("mcp__s__mem","context_write","ask"), ("mcp__s__box","sandbox_compute","ask") and ("mcp__s__own","read","durable_owner"). Under Off and Shadow, the read/ask MCP view is false (legacy) and READ_TOOL with any view is true (legacy). Using the Counted recorder pattern of mod.rs:1830-1892, assert Shadow records `tool_class_divergence_total{point=disclosure_consent,tool=mcp__}` for the external_write/ask MCP view: today declared=true and legacy=false, so it counts; after the fix it counts nothing. Assert it records nothing for that view after the fix, and exactly one `tool=read_subagent_result` divergence for READ_TOOL with view (READ_TOOL,"external_write","none",""), the drift signal the call-site OR must not hide.
- agent.rs test module, near 15433: new test `under_enforce_an_ask_floor_on_a_risky_or_unclassified_class_is_labelled_destructive_and_a_read_ask_floor_a_disclosure`. Call permission::record_run_views with a unique org/run ("org-d1-273-kind", "run-d1-273-kind") for mcp__srv__lookup read/ask, mcp__srv__pay external_write/ask, mcp__srv__mystery unclassified/none, and READ_TOOL external_write/none. With RunGate::with_gate(Enforce, org, run): lookup gives Permission and the generic disclosure reason (contains "into this conversation", does not contain "requires approval" or "subagent"). pay and mystery give Destructive and "tool 'X' requires approval". READ_TOOL gives Permission and the exact subagent sentence, because the view cannot remove a reserved name. With RunGate::with_gate(Off, org, run): lookup gives Destructive and "tool 'mcp__srv__lookup' requires approval", and READ_TOOL gives Permission. With Enforce for another run id (no snapshot), every result is the legacy answer.
- runtime_loop/mod.rs test module, next to the test at 3811-3850: new test `the_pause_cause_names_a_disclosure_only_for_a_read_ask_floor_or_a_reserved_name`. Use the same recording pattern with a unique org/run ("org-d1-273-cause", "run-d1-273-cause"). Under Enforce: read/ask MCP gives ConsentToDisclose; external_write/ask MCP gives RiskyEffectUnderAsk; unclassified/none MCP gives RiskyEffectUnderAsk; execute_provider_action with view external_write/ask gives ProviderWrite; read/durable_owner MCP gives OwnerEffectReserved; READ_TOOL with view external_write/none gives ConsentToDisclose. Under Off: read/ask MCP gives RiskyEffectUnderAsk and READ_TOOL gives ConsentToDisclose.

Must NOT change: any PermissionDecision (pause or no pause) on any posture; the owner marker logic and its call sites (grpc.rs, resume.rs, continuation_descriptor's owner check); grpc.rs at all, including the ExecuteStep approval at grpc.rs:1479 and 1483, which is a separate follow-up; ToolClassGate parsing or its default (off, strict literal parser); proto, Go, SQL migrations, env, compose; CauseCode variants; the existing reason strings. Preserve CRLF working-tree line endings in all four files (index is LF, worktree CRLF). Do not run git checkout/reset/stash/commit or docker. The lead commits and updates the register and ledger.

packets.title: Go cross-service contract: broker acceptsReasoningEffort matches inference-core CODEX_LEVELS / CODEX_WIDE_LEVELS
packets.brief:
Create ONE new test file in package codexsubscription. It is an internal test, in the same package as manager_test.go, which defines fakeRunner; manager_test.go:101 already builds NewManager(Config{Enabled:true, Home:t.TempDir(), WideReasoningEffort:tc.wide}, runner). Follow the pattern of internal/api/codex_subscription_contract_test.go:33-50, and the Rust apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/tests/cross_service_loop_contract.rs for the 'mutate, then show it goes red when either side drifts' style.

(1) Reading the source. Set effortModelPlaneDir := filepath.Join("..","..","..","..","Model Plane"); from internal/codexsubscription this resolves to apps/Model Plane. Do not reuse the name modelPlaneDir, so the test stays clear of package api. If os.Stat fails, call t.Skipf. Otherwise read rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/effort.rs. On a read error, call t.Fatalf with a message saying to re-point the path and not delete the test. Normalise \r\n to \n.

(2) Parsing the ladders. Use regexps anchored at line start, so the comment lines at effort.rs:158-162, which name both constants in prose, never match:
(?m)^[ \t]*(?:pub(?:\([^)]*\))?\s+)?const\s+CODEX_LEVELS\s*:\s*&\[Level\]\s*=\s*&\[([^\]]*)\]\s*;
Use the same pattern for CODEX_WIDE_LEVELS. Today both are private consts on one line each (:160 and :163). Extract the Level::(\w+) variants. Fail if a list is not found, is empty, or the regexp matches more than once.

(3) Parsing the wire names. effort.rs has exactly one as_str, at :65 inside impl Level at :51. Parse the body of `pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {` up to the closing brace of its match, using Level::(\w+)\s*=>\s*"([a-z]+)", into a map from variant to wire name. Fail if any ladder variant has no mapping.

(4) Write a pure helper effortViolations(ladder []string, accepts func(string) bool, universe []string) []string. It reports every ladder wire name that accepts rejects, and every universe name that accepts admits but the ladder lacks. The universe is every as_str value plus "maximum", "none", "ultra" and "". The empty string is rejected by acceptsReasoningEffort; the defaulting to "low" happens earlier, in manager.go:430-432.

(5) Tests. Use manager.acceptsReasoningEffort as accepts.
- TestBrokerPairMatchesInferenceCoreCodexLevels: wide=false against CODEX_LEVELS.
- TestWideBrokerMatchesInferenceCoreCodexWideLevels: wide=true against CODEX_WIDE_LEVELS.
- TestBrokerDefaultEffortIsOnTheInferenceCoreLadder: "low" is in the rendered CODEX_LEVELS and is accepted with wide off. This pins the broker default (manager.go:430-432) and inference-core's default (codex_subscription.rs:190-192).
- TestEffortContractGoesRedWhenEitherSideDrifts. Write mutate(t, text, from, to). It must t.Fatalf unless strings.Count(text, from) == 1. Mutation (a) must use the WHOLE declaration line as from, because the fragments `, Level::XHigh` and `Level::High, Level::XHigh]` also appear in the test at effort.rs:725: from = `const CODEX_WIDE_LEVELS: &[Level] = &[Level::Low, Level::Medium, Level::High, Level::XHigh];`, to = the same line without `, Level::XHigh`. Re-parse the mutated text and check it against the wide manager; it must give violations. (b) An accepts that also admits "max" must give violations against CODEX_WIDE_LEVELS. (c) A wide accepts that drops "medium" must give violations.

No env reads, no network, no t.Setenv. Put a doc comment at the top saying three things: the test reads source because the two sides are separate languages and deploy separately; it runtime-asserts the broker half; and it closes D1-725 and D1-730. gofmt the file. The index stores LF and the checkout has CRLF; either is fine for go, so match the siblings.

These tests PASS on today's tree by design, because they pin the current agreement. The proof that they work is TestEffortContractGoesRedWhenEitherSideDrifts.

MUST NOT change: manager.go or any non-test file, existing tests, config defaults, any .env file, or internal/api.

packets.title: imports-core: local Tesseract OCR for scanned PDFs on the ephemeral extract route, default off
packets.brief:
Add local OCR to imports-core's in-memory chat extract route, for PDFs with no text layer. Today such a PDF gets a 422 'No readable text found. Scanned files require a text version.' (app/chat_extract.py:61-62).

(1) NEW app/ocr.py
- `ocr_enabled()`: True only when os.getenv('CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_ENABLED') == 'true' exactly. Read it on every call.
- `max_pages()`: CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_MAX_PAGES. Accept a decimal integer from 1 to 50; anything else gives 15.
- Constants: DEADLINE_S = 18.0 (CHATGAP OD18; stays under the BFF's 25 s client timeout) and PAGE_TIMEOUT_S = 10.
- Concurrency: a module-level threading.BoundedSemaphore(1), because imports-api is limited to 256M and 0.25 CPU. Acquire it with a 2 s timeout, or raise OcrUnavailableError.
- `ocr_pdf(content: bytes) -> OcrResult(text: str, pages_read: int, pages_total: int)`:
  - Count pages with pypdf.PdfReader.
  - Work inside tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='ocr-'), and write in.pdf there.
  - For i in 1..min(total, max_pages), stop when the monotonic deadline has passed. For each page:
    - Render it alone: `pdftoppm -r 200 -gray -png -f i -l i -singlefile in.pdf p<i>`.
    - Then run `tesseract p<i>.png stdout -l eng+nor --psm 3`.
  - Every subprocess call goes through one seam, `_run(argv, timeout)`, which calls subprocess.run(argv, shell=False, capture_output=True, timeout=min(PAGE_TIMEOUT_S, remaining), env={'PATH': os.environ.get('PATH',''), 'OMP_THREAD_LIMIT': '1'}, check=False).
  - If page 1 hits FileNotFoundError, a non-zero exit or TimeoutExpired, raise OcrUnavailableError. If a later page hits one, stop and return the pages read so far.
  - Join page texts with '\n\f\n'.
- Logging and errors: never put stderr, stdout or document text in an exception message or a log line. At most one INFO line, with pages_read, pages_total and elapsed ms.

(2) app/chat_extract.py: change only the empty-text branch (:61-62)
Apply this when the suffix is 'pdf' and ocr_enabled():
- OcrUnavailableError gives HTTPException(422, 'The scanned file could not be read. Try a text version.').
- If the OCR text is empty, keep the existing 422 message.
- If pages_read < pages_total, append the marker '\n\n[Read the first {pages_read} of {pages_total} pages. The rest was not read.]'. That is chat-path truncation per OD18, same as the xlsx precedent at :66-68.
- Then apply the existing 60,000-character check (413), unchanged.
- Return the same envelope plus data['ocr'] = True, and data['truncated'] = True when truncated.
- When the switch is off, behaviour is byte-identical to today.
- Docstring: local, no network, nothing persisted; this does not change the ZDR attachment refusal elsewhere.

(3) Dockerfile, runtime stage only
After the ENV block that ends at line 24, and before `RUN addgroup` (:26), add one line: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng tesseract-ocr-nor poppler-utils && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*.

(4) apps/Ingestion Plane/docker-compose.yml, imports-api environment
After TIKA_TIMEOUT_S (around :367), add:
- CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_ENABLED: ${CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_ENABLED:-false}
- CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_MAX_PAGES: ${CHAT_EXTRACT_OCR_MAX_PAGES:-15}
Do not change the resource limits.

(5) NEW tests/test_chat_extract_ocr.py
Use pytest and call extract_chat_document directly, as test_chat_extract.py:8 does. Monkeypatch app.ocr._run and the environment. Build blank PDFs with pypdf PdfWriter().add_blank_page(200, 200).
(a) Switch unset or set to 'TRUE', '1' or ' true': the old 422 message, and _run is never called.

No. Render text with `tesseract`? No. Use poppler's absence of a writer instead: skip unless tests/fixtures/scanned-sample.pdf exists. The lead supplies that file.

1) thinking.rs. Add `#[must_use] pub fn run_level(profile: &str, ladder_on: bool) -> i32`: `effort_level(profile) as i32` when ladder_on, 0 otherwise. Reuse effort_level (thinking.rs:131); never write a second mapping. Unit tests:
- deep_is_high_with_the_ladder_on (4);
- anything_is_unspecified_with_the_ladder_off;
- standard_and_unset_are_unspecified.

2) sse.rs:
(a) build_run_agent_request's full literal (10351-10421): add `reasoning_effort: mp_contracts::model_plane::v1::ReasoningEffort::Unspecified as i32,` with the comment "set by resolved_run_agent_request for a fresh run". The function stays pure and its signature unchanged, so the `build` helpers at 872-905 keep giving 0.
(b) resolved_run_agent_request (10281). Its doc (10278-10279) says it is "the one place a dispatch's request is made", so the level goes here. Add `run_effort: i32` as the last parameter. Capture `let fresh = resume.is_none();` before resume moves. Return `RunAgentRequest { reasoning_effort: if fresh { run_effort } else { 0 }, ..build_run_agent_request(...) }`, with a comment that a continuation segment carries no level.
(c) Thread `run_effort: i32` as the last parameter through spawn_run_dispatch (10069; its only caller is 10919) to the resolved_run_agent_request call at 10173, and through agentic_run_stream (10787) to the spawn_run_dispatch call at 10919.
(d) The production call at 1896 passes `crate::thinking::run_level(req.effort.as_deref().unwrap_or_default(), crate::thinking::ladder_enabled())`. req.effort is already clamped by the org cap at 1250, in the same function, so the run inherits the clamp.
(e) Test callers: agentic_run_stream at 16633, 18470 and 19782, and resolved_run_agent_request at 16928 (continue_run_agent_request). All pass 0.
(f) New lib tests, next to the continue_run_agent_request tests (~16919):
- a_fresh_do_run_carries_the_turn_level: resolved_run_agent_request with resume None and run_effort 4 gives 4.
- a_continuation_carries_no_level: Some(resume) and run_effort 4 gives 0.
- the_pure_builder_sends_no_level: `build(...)` gives 0.

3) tests/effort_ladder_contract.rs (source-text test). Add do_run_level_uses_the_one_derivation: sse.rs's `return agentic_run_stream(` call uses `thinking::run_level`, and sse.rs has no `"deep" =>` style profile match outside thinking.rs.

The source-scan tests in sse.rs (14594, 17071, 19158-19251, 20389-20439) must stay green: count of `agentic_run_stream(` == 1 in the launch body, the `resolved_run_agent_request(` find, the `spawn_run_dispatch(` find. If one pins exact call text, update only that assertion's expected text and say so in the report.

Must NOT change:
- the chat answer's effort derivation (sse.rs ~3158-3192, 9160-9165);
- ZDR turn settings and the budget or admission order;
- the tool-loop decision rounds (tool_loop.rs effort stays 0);
- AgentRoute semantics.
Add no new gateway switch: the field is inert unless the executor's switch is on.

packets.brief:
UPDATE after commit 73906fa6e (the Claude 5.5 adapter): the line numbers below moved. apply_thinking is now anthropic.rs:712-764; the legacy branch is 716-726, the no-room guard 736-743, the `_ => return` arm 761, and `body["max_tokens"] = serde_json::json!(max_tokens);` is line 763 (still the right place for the log). The ladder now also runs for every Claude 5.5 model whatever the switch says (is_claude_5_5), and a 5.5 request naming no level resolves to the model default, so add a third test a_claude_5_5_request_logs_its_default_level (claude-sonnet-5-5, no level: one line whose applied equals claude_5_5_default_effort's level). The body tests now sit around 3000-3310. Find items by name, not by the old numbers.

anthropic.rs is CRLF. In apply_thinking (605-654), ladder branch only, emit one `info!` with the same fields as openai.rs:502-511 and codex_subscription.rs:136-144:
- request_id = %req.request_id
- model = %req.model
- wire = ?resolved.wire
- requested = resolved.requested.as_str()
- applied = resolved.applied.as_str()
- clamped = resolved.clamped()
- max_tokens
- message "effort_resolved"

Place it immediately before `body["max_tokens"] = serde_json::json!(max_tokens);` (653). That line is reached only after a thinking block was written. Do not place it right after resolve_ladder_effort: then a budget dropped by the no-room guard (626-632) or the `_ => return` arm would log a level that was never sent. Log ids and closed tokens only: no prompt, no content.

Test (required). A capture pattern exists in codex_subscription_tools.rs:1140: a `Recorder` subscriber used with tracing::subscriber::with_default. Reuse it locally in anthropic.rs's test module, without a new dependency, and add:
- anthropic_ladder_logs_effort_resolved_once_per_body: one line with applied=high for a High request on a Budget-class model, and none of the user text in it.
- a_dropped_budget_logs_no_effort_resolved: a max_tokens so small that the guard omits the thinking block, and no effort_resolved line.

Must NOT change: any request body (the golden and body tests at ~1547-1943 and 2863-2881 stay green), adaptive_thinking_flag_enabled, resolve_thinking_budget, or the legacy branch (606-615).
